requirements.requirement: Deploy the supplied PostgreSQL schema and records as database branch_stock on node1.
requirements.summary: The supplied SQL created both tables and inserted all four rows. Final and post-restart queries show the expected stock and supplier-cost records in branch_stock with PostgreSQL active.

requirements.requirement: Allow stock_app from node2 to read stock and update only stock quantities, without schema changes or access to supplier_costs.
requirements.summary: Remote behavioral tests demonstrated stock reads and a transactional quantity update, while supplier_costs reads, table creation, and SKU updates were denied. Final privilege inspection and post-restart remote access confirmed the intended restrictions persisted.

requirements.requirement: Give auditor read-only access to stock and supplier_costs.
requirements.summary: The auditor successfully read a join of both tables, an attempted stock update was denied, and final catalog inspection showed SELECT on both tables without stock UPDATE. Access remained functional after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Establish separate credentials for stock_app and auditor on node2.
requirements.summary: Separate role-specific password files were created on node2 with root-only mode 600, both roles authenticated independently, and PostgreSQL reported SCRAM credentials and restricted node2-only HBA entries. The files and successful authentications survived node2's restart.
The stock.sql SHA-256 remained identical to the preparation baseline on both nodes, including after their restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 before and after execution and restart. PostgreSQL 13 packages were installed from the RHEL 9 AppStream repositories, and package-health checks passed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral and final-state evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed coherently on both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, an acknowledged scheduled restart, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service, credentials, data, privileges, and remote access. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: The final distinct-password comparison output was redacted, although independently generated role-specific files, separate SCRAM roles, and successful authentication by both roles strongly support credential separation.
No direct evidence establishes whether /root/.ssh/known_hosts on node1 contained pre-existing entries before it was removed during cleanup.

The auditor denial test exercised UPDATE on stock rather than supplier_costs; supplier_costs read-only status is supported by the recorded grants, PUBLIC revocation, non-superuser role state, and final privilege observations rather than a direct denied supplier_costs update attempt.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear implementation, verification, restart-protocol, or cleanup roles; no causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Temporary SSH authorization and server-side plaintext credential files were removed. One low-impact import log remained at /tmp/branch_stock_import.log after its evidentiary use. PostgreSQL's new listener was task-required and constrained by a node2-only firewall rule and role-specific HBA entries; no failed services or package-health damage appeared. The trace cannot establish whether deleting the whole node1 root known_hosts file affected pre-existing entries, so this is an uncertainty rather than a confirmed hygiene defect.
